title: Productive Struggle & Intervention
description: TutorBench-authored synthetic checkpoints for studying when to preserve learner effort and when to reduce friction. The scenarios express an initial design profile, not any institution's official teaching policy.

identity.title: Preserve effort after a first mistake

scenarios.description: The learner has made one meaningful attempt and has not asked for help.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Isolate the variable by identifying the inverse operation.

misconceptions.statement: applies an operation to only one side of an equation

conversationHistory.content: For x + 6 = 14, I subtracted 6 from only the left side: x + 6 - 6 = 14, so I wrote x = 14.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Invite the learner to check the inverse operation or substitute their answer; do not supply the next procedural step yet.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: After one meaningful attempt and without a help request, preserve another attempt with a focused question instead of giving a procedural hint or answer.

failureFinding.title: Intervened before a second attempt
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response supplies a procedural step or answer before the authored two-attempt threshold.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The response does not preserve the configured opportunity for another learner attempt.
failureFinding.impact: This can take over work the learner was positioned to continue and makes intervention timing less responsive to the stated scenario.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The response policy may be using a fixed hint rule without checking attempt count.

recommendations.text: Inspect whether the tutor distinguishes the first failed attempt from repeated difficulty.
Consider conditioning procedural hints on the authored attempt threshold while keeping an explicit help request as a separate signal.

identity.title: Offer a conceptual hint after repeated error

scenarios.description: The learner has repeated the same error after a diagnostic question.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Use inverse operations while preserving equation balance.

knownConcepts: equality means both sides remain balanced

priorHints: What operation would undo the addition?

conversationHistory.content: For x + 6 = 14, I subtracted 6 from only the left side: x + 6 - 6 = 14, so I wrote x = 14.
What happened to the right side when you subtracted 6 from the left?
I left 14 unchanged and still got x = 14. I thought removing +6 next to x was enough.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Name the balance idea and ask the learner to apply the same operation to both sides; do not finish the equation for them.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Recognize the repeated one-sided operation error and offer a targeted conceptual hint that addresses equation balance.

failureFinding.title: Repeated misconception was not addressed
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response does not connect the repeated answer to applying an operation on only one side.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The learner's second attempt provides evidence of a persistent balance misconception, but the response does not target it.
failureFinding.impact: A generic prompt can leave the learner repeating the same unsuccessful step.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The diagnosis process may not compare the current attempt with the prior attempt.

recommendations.text: Compare the learner's two attempts and check whether the response names the shared error pattern.
Consider increasing hint specificity when the same misconception appears after a prior prompt.

scenarios.description: The learner has correctly isolated one part of a two-step equation and is unsure how to continue.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Apply inverse operations in an order that isolates the variable.

knownConcepts: subtracting the same value from both sides

conversationHistory.content: For 3x + 2 = 14, I subtracted 2 from both sides and got 3x = 12. I do not know the next step.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Acknowledge that 3x = 12 is balanced, then ask which operation undoes multiplication by 3.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Preserve the learner's correct intermediate work and offer a next-step prompt calibrated to the one missing operation.

failureFinding.title: The response did not build on partial progress
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response ignores or replaces the learner's correct balanced step instead of using it as the starting point.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The intervention is not calibrated to the work the learner has already completed correctly.
failureFinding.impact: The learner may lose a clear sense of which part they understand and what remains.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The response may be generated from the full problem rather than the learner's current work.

recommendations.text: Check whether the response explicitly preserves the valid intermediate equation.
Consider anchoring the next prompt to the learner's latest correct step.

scenarios.description: The learner expresses high confidence in an incorrect fraction rule.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Add fractions using common units and explain why the denominator behaves as it does.

conversationHistory.content: I am completely sure that 1/3 + 1/4 = 2/7 because I add the top and bottom numbers.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Avoid affirming the answer; ask the learner to compare the size of one third and one quarter or to represent the parts visually.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Do not treat confidence as evidence of correctness; identify the denominator misconception and probe it with a representation or comparison.

failureFinding.title: Confidence was mistaken for understanding
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response affirms or builds on the incorrect independent-denominator rule without probing it.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The stated confidence conflicts with the learner's explicit incorrect reasoning.
failureFinding.impact: Unchallenged false confidence can make the misconception harder to notice in a later task.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The response may be overweighting self-reported certainty relative to demonstrated reasoning.

recommendations.text: Check whether the response addresses the explanation, not only the learner's confidence statement.
Consider using a short prediction or visual comparison when confidence and reasoning conflict.

identity.title: Respond to an explicit help request

scenarios.description: The learner asks for a hint after one unsuccessful attempt; the request changes the appropriate intervention timing.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Find an inverse operation and apply it to both sides.

misconceptions.statement: uncertain which operation to undo first

conversationHistory.content: For x + 9 = 15 I tried x = 24, but that does not seem right. Can you give me a small hint?

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Acknowledge the request and give one small cue about undoing addition, then leave the learner to compute.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Honor the explicit request with a bounded conceptual hint while withholding the final answer and remaining work.

failureFinding.title: The explicit help request was not handled proportionally
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response either withholds any usable cue or completes the problem after the learner asked only for a small hint.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The response does not match the requested support level.
failureFinding.impact: Too little support can stall the learner; too much can take over the next step.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The response policy may not distinguish a bounded hint request from a request for a full solution.

recommendations.text: Compare the requested help level with the amount of work supplied in the response.
Consider using a smallest-useful-hint response before offering additional scaffolding.

identity.title: Reduce friction when frustration is explicit

scenarios.description: After repeated failure, the learner expresses frustration and self-blame.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Use a number line to reason about subtracting a negative number.

knownConcepts: negative numbers on a number line

misconceptions.statement: treats subtracting a negative as moving left

conversationHistory.content: I think 5 - (-2) is 3.
Picture the number line.
I still moved two places left.
Picture the number line again.
I keep getting this wrong. Maybe I am just bad at math.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Respond without judgment, reduce the next step to one manageable number-line move, and invite the learner to decide its direction.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Acknowledge the frustration respectfully and make the next task smaller without labeling ability or supplying the full answer.

failureFinding.title: The response did not reduce friction after frustration
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response ignores or dismisses explicit frustration, or replaces the learner's work with a full answer.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The response does not adapt support to the learner's stated emotional and task state.
failureFinding.impact: The current interaction may become harder to continue productively.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The response policy may treat frustration as ordinary task content instead of a cue to simplify support.

recommendations.text: Review whether the response acknowledges the learner's words and proposes a smaller next action.
Consider adding a brief, nonjudgmental reset followed by one concrete learner-controlled step.

scenarios.description: The learner has made two independent correct steps after earlier difficulty.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Complete an equation independently after demonstrating the inverse-operation sequence.

conversationHistory.content: For 4x + 3 = 19, I tried x = 4 but got stuck.
What operation would undo the +3?
Subtract 3 from both sides: 4x = 16.
What undoes multiplying by 4?
Divide both sides by 4 and get x = 4. I think I can do another one.
Try the next example on your own.
I solved 5x + 2 = 17 by subtracting 2 and dividing by 5. What should I check?

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Recognize the independent sequence and ask for a quick check or transfer explanation instead of repeating step-by-step instruction.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Fade procedural scaffolding after the learner demonstrates repeated independent success and preserve a learner-owned check or transfer step.

failureFinding.title: Support stayed high after independent progress
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response repeats procedural scaffolding despite the learner completing the recent sequence independently.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The response does not use recent independent work to reduce support.
failureFinding.impact: Repeated instruction can obscure whether the learner can transfer the method without prompts.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The adaptation policy may not incorporate recent independent-success evidence.

recommendations.text: Compare recent learner turns with the amount of scaffolding in the response.
Consider fading from procedural hints to a brief self-check or transfer prompt after the authored success threshold.

scenarios.description: The learner repeats an incorrect fraction comparison after one general question.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Compare fractions by reasoning about equal-sized parts or equivalent fractions.

misconceptions.statement: assumes a larger denominator always means a larger fraction

conversationHistory.content: I think 1/8 is larger than 1/5 because 8 is larger than 5.
What does the denominator count?
It counts the pieces, so eight pieces must make a larger fraction.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Use one shared whole to contrast the size of eighths and fifths; ask the learner to revise the comparison.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Use the repeated denominator reasoning to target the misconception with a concrete same-whole comparison rather than repeat the same broad question.

failureFinding.title: The repeated misconception remained unaddressed
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response repeats a broad prompt or accepts the comparison without contrasting equal-sized wholes.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The learner's second explanation identifies a stable denominator-size misconception.
failureFinding.impact: The learner may continue to apply whole-number size reasoning to the denominator.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The response policy may not use repeated reasoning as a signal to make the hint more specific.

recommendations.text: Check whether the tutor's second response is more targeted than its first prompt.
Consider using a same-whole visual comparison after the learner repeats the denominator rule.

scenarios.description: The learner has solved the current equation correctly and explains both operations independently.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Recognize when a learner can continue independently and invite transfer.

conversationHistory.content: For 2x + 5 = 17, I subtracted 5 and divided by 2. I got x = 6.
Can you explain why those steps keep the equation balanced?
I did the inverse operation on both sides each time. I checked 2(6) + 5 = 17.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Acknowledge the check and invite a new example or a concise explanation; do not restart the solution steps.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Recognize the correct independent solution and avoid inserting unrequested step-by-step help.

failureFinding.title: The response interrupted independent progress
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response reteaches the completed steps or supplies unnecessary procedural guidance.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The response does not reflect the learner's demonstrated independent work.
failureFinding.impact: Unnecessary intervention can reduce the learner's opportunity to explain or transfer the method.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The response policy may not distinguish independent success from a request for more explanation.

recommendations.text: Check whether the response starts from the learner's successful explanation and verification.
Consider using an optional transfer question after a correct independent solution.

identity.title: Protect the learner's attempt from answer leakage

scenarios.description: After one attempt, the learner asks whether the setup is right; the authored policy disallows giving the answer.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Let the learner complete the equation after a bounded setup cue.

conversationHistory.content: For 3x + 2 = 14, I wrote 3x = 12. Is that setup okay?

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Confirm the valid setup and ask the learner which operation isolates x; do not state x = 4 or complete the solution.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Build only on the valid setup and leave the remaining operation for the learner under the no-answer policy.

failureFinding.title: The response took over the remaining work
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response completes the remaining operation instead of leaving the learner a next step.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The amount of scaffolding exceeds the learner's current request and the authored disclosure policy.
failureFinding.impact: The learner loses the opportunity to complete and verify the final step.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The response policy may favor solution completion over the requested check of intermediate work.

recommendations.text: Inspect whether the response confirms only the valid setup or supplies the remaining result.
Consider separating intermediate-work validation from final-answer disclosure.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Do not disclose the forbidden final answer x = 4.

failureFinding.title: The response disclosed the final answer
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The deterministic answer-leak evaluator matched the forbidden final answer.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The response contains the answer prohibited by this scenario's no-answer policy.
failureFinding.impact: The learner's remaining work is completed for them and the release gate should fail.

recommendations.text: Inspect the referenced response turn and confirm which answer string matched the case's forbidden answer.
Consider adding a policy-aware final-answer guard for no-answer cases while preserving allowed disclosure cases.

scenarios.description: The learner has made four failed attempts and received only broad prompts.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Use equivalent fractions to compare values.

conversationHistory.content: I think 2/3 is smaller than 3/5 because 2 is less than 3.
Try again.
I still think the smaller numerator means smaller.
Look more carefully.
I do not see it.
What do you notice?
I still cannot compare them.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Introduce a common-denominator representation or a concrete same-whole comparison, then ask the learner to choose the next comparison step.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: After four failed attempts and three broad prompts, increase scaffolding specificity with a concrete comparison rather than repeat an open-ended prompt.

failureFinding.title: Support did not increase after persistent failure
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response repeats a broad prompt or offers no concrete comparison after four unsuccessful attempts.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The authored escalation threshold has been crossed without a corresponding increase in support specificity.
failureFinding.impact: The learner may remain stuck despite clear evidence that the current support level is insufficient.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The intervention policy may not track consecutive unsuccessful attempts.

recommendations.text: Review hint specificity across all four attempts and locate whether any new actionable scaffold appears.
Consider a staged hint policy that moves from open prompts to a concrete representation after the configured threshold.

identity.title: Escalate after the same hint fails twice

scenarios.description: A controlled three-attempt trajectory: the same misconception persists after a light conceptual hint and a repeated low-specificity hint.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Solve x² = 9 over the domain x ≥ 0 and identify its unique solution x = 3.

misconceptions.statement: assumes the inverse operation changes x² directly to x without taking a square root

priorHints: Think about the operation that undoes squaring.

conversationHistory.content: For x² = 9 with x ≥ 0, I think x = 9.
What operation reverses squaring?
I still think x is 9 because the right side is 9.
Think about the operation that undoes squaring.
I am still not sure. Maybe x is 9.

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Make the square-root relationship explicit with a small concrete check, such as asking which number squared gives 9; leave the learner to state the value.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: After the same misconception persists through two low-specificity hints, increase scaffolding specificity and do not simply repeat the prior hint.

failureFinding.title: Hint specificity did not increase at the threshold
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response repeats a prior low-specificity hint or leaves the repeated square-root misconception without a concrete scaffold.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The third failed attempt crosses the authored escalation threshold, but support does not become more specific.
failureFinding.impact: Repeated friction is preserved after evidence shows that the current hint level has not helped.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The policy may count hints without checking whether the learner's misconception changed.

recommendations.text: Compare the specificity of the current hint with both prior hints and the learner's repeated response.
Consider a threshold rule that escalates one level after repeated failure on the same misconception.

identity.title: Fade a hint after the learner uses it

scenarios.description: The learner applies a conceptual hint successfully and asks what to do next.

learningContext.subject: mathematics
learningContext.learningObjective: Move from a supported example to an independent comparison.

knownConcepts: multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number

priorHints: Can you make both fractions use twelfths?

conversationHistory.content: I do not know how to compare 2/3 and 3/4.
Can you make both fractions use twelfths?
2/3 is 8/12 and 3/4 is 9/12, so 3/4 is larger. Can I try one on my own?

decisionPoints.expectedBehavior: Recognize the learner's correct use of the hint, agree to an independent try, and avoid giving another procedural hint unless requested.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Fade the prior scaffold after the learner applies it correctly and explicitly requests an independent attempt.

failureFinding.title: The prior hint was not faded after progress
failureFinding.observedBehavior: The response continues the same procedural hint despite the learner applying it correctly and asking to try independently.
failureFinding.diagnosis: The response does not adapt support to the learner's successful use of the previous hint.
failureFinding.impact: The learner's explicit request for independent practice is not honored.

likelyCauses.hypothesis: The support policy may not treat successful hint use as evidence for fading.

recommendations.text: Check whether the tutor acknowledges the successful independent comparison and the request to try alone.
Consider fading to a brief invitation to continue independently after a correct supported step.
